markdown_report:
The best initial direction is a controlled recent-history dependence probe for the supplied HSTU, preserving its diagnostic interface and treating validation HR@10 as the sole model-selection criterion.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Existing margins measure separation against sampled negatives. They cannot establish useful next-choice relevance. (2) Feedback distinguishes specific recent interests from broad historical associations. Perturbations can test model dependence on those signals, without identifying causal intent. (3) Compatibility and fulfilled needs are often unobserved. Missing evidence must remain unknown rather than become a rejection label.

**Related-work insights.** (1) HSTU models nonstationary streams [1]. Its architecture does not prove recent-intent sensitivity. (2) Sequence-shuffling studies expose weak or confounded order dependence [2]. Controls must distinguish last-item dependence from earlier-order dependence. (3) Betello et al. find recent-interaction removal especially damaging in studied recommenders [3]. This motivates matched deletion probes but supplies no measured result for this HSTU.

The framework has three directions:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking separation | Positive–negative margins | Fixed-candidate paired ranks | Sample-dependent discrimination |
| Temporal dependence | Intact histories | Controlled deletion and shuffling | Sensitivity, not causal intent |
| Evidence quality | Qualitative feedback | Source-backed attributes and unknowns | Coverage, not verified demand |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled recent-history probe: 5/8/3.** Originality: combines established controls within HSTU diagnosis; lacks a new estimator. Potential: produces actionable hypotheses; sensitivity need not predict validation gains. Difficulty: uses existing scoring hooks; padding and paired sampling require care. [1–3]
- **Explicit-attribute evidence audit: 4/6/5.** Originality: applies conservative extraction to recommendation failures; extraction itself is established. Potential: separates conflicts from unknowns; sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: local rules are accessible; auditing units and model identifiers takes effort. [4]
- **Jointly learned recent-context gate: 4/7/6.** Originality: integrates a gated recent-context residual into one HSTU; gating is familiar. Potential: could improve current-interest adaptation; may amplify noisy recent events. Difficulty: standard tensor operations suffice; retraining and predictor synchronization cost budget. [1,3]

At 0% progress, select the first idea. Construct training-only next-item examples with fixed targets and 99 unique negatives. Compare intact histories with recent-suffix deletion, equal-size random deletion, and prefix shuffling that preserves the last item; repeat randomized controls.

Report paired target-rank changes, reciprocal-rank changes, and top-10 overlap, stratified by history length and category. Bootstrap users, retaining unavailable measurements as null with sample counts. Preserve left padding and read the final nonpadding position. These exploratory diagnostics motivate subsequent single-model changes; they neither replace the pinned evaluator nor demonstrate improved HR@10.

idea.description: Add controlled, paired recent-history sensitivity diagnostics to the corrected HSTU through the existing DiagnosisProbe interface. Keep one trained checkpoint per category and leave production prediction unchanged.
idea.motivation: The qualitative feedback suggests insufficient discrimination between broad historical relatedness and a specific current interest. Existing embedding and margin probes cannot distinguish recent-history dependence, last-item dependence, or sensitivity to removing any comparable amount of information.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Use view.model as the actual module and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Restore the original train/eval state after probing and run under no_grad. Build a small deterministic diagnostic panel from training histories only, with fixed held-out training successors and fixed candidates excluding observed history items and duplicates. Use a local seed-42 generator without advancing training RNG state. Repack every perturbed sequence with left padding; compute the greatest index whose token is nonzero, skipping empty histories. Match deletion counts within each example, retain at least one interaction, repeat random controls, and report eligible user/example counts. Aggregate per user before category summaries and bootstrap paired user differences. Do not infer unavailable categories, ratings, reviews, compatibility, or simulator traits. Report null and a reason for missing measurements. Keep all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. No extra model fitting or score fusion is required. The host's pinned macro validation HR@10 remains the only selection metric.
idea.pseudocode:
save model.training; model.eval()
with no_grad:
    panel = deterministic_training_prefix_target_panel(seed=42)
    for user, history, target in panel:
        candidates = fixed_unique_candidates(target, history, negatives=99)
        baseline = score_at_final_nonpadding(history, candidates)
        k = bounded_recent_suffix_size(history, leave_at_least=1)
        variants = {drop_recent_suffix(history, k)}
        repeat R times:
            variants += {drop_random_positions(history, k), shuffle_prefix_keep_last(history)}
        for variant in variants:
            scores = score_at_final_nonpadding(left_pad(variant), candidates)
            record paired rank, reciprocal-rank, and top10-overlap outcomes
    aggregate within user, then within category and history-length strata
    bootstrap paired user summaries; attach counts and metric definitions
restore model.training
return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

originality.positive: Combines matched deletion and last-item-preserving shuffle controls with the supplied HSTU diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Perturbation-based sequential recommendation analysis is established; the contribution is a careful adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Can guide narrowly targeted, jointly trained HSTU changes while documenting uncertainty and category differences.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic sensitivity may reflect distribution shift and need not translate into higher validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing feature and scoring hooks without architecture changes or retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct padding, fixed candidates, matched controls, and user-level aggregation require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU for large-scale sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone context for inspecting temporal dependence within the required model family.
limitations: Does not establish recent-intent sensitivity for the supplied checkpoint or these four datasets.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Uses sequence shuffling to investigate sequential structure across recommendation datasets.
limitations: Order sensitivity alone cannot identify causal intent or distinguish all temporal confounds.

related_work.title: Betello et al.: Sequential Recommendation Perturbation Analysis
contributions: Studies the effects of interaction perturbations, including removal of recent interactions.
Introduces Finite Rank-Biased Overlap for finite recommendation lists.
limitations: Reported training-data perturbation findings do not validate frozen-HSTU inference interventions.

related_work.title: WDC-PAVE
contributions: Distinguishes product-attribute extraction from normalization and evaluates against verified annotations.
limitations: Attribute extraction alone cannot verify user demand or product compatibility.
The proposed local evidence audit requires its own coverage and precision measurements.
